tagline: AI content, smart scheduling, engagement tools, and analytics for growing on X.
verdictSummary: The personal core — a composer with an LLM writing in your own voice, a slot-based scheduler, basic post-metrics tracking — is a weekend build, the same as every other social scheduler in this catalogue. What isn't buildable: X's write API costs real money before your first scheduled post even goes out, the viral-post library and timing models are proprietary data collected over years, and engagement automations sit in rate-limit and terms-of-service territory a personal script will get wrong.
coreLoopDIY: Compose posts and threads with an LLM prompted on samples of your own past writing, queue them into weekday time slots, publish through the X API, and pull your own post metrics into a local dashboard.
whatYouLose: a large viral-post library and niche inspiration feed
whyPeopleStillPay: X's API meters every write before your first post goes out, so the DIY version starts with a monthly API bill and none of the product. What actually grows an account — knowing what performs in your niche, and when — comes from data collected and modeled over years, not from code you can regenerate.
notes: Judged by the same rubric as every other entry here: real capability, real cost, no exceptions made.
prompt:
Build a personal X posting cockpit: a composer with an AI draft panel that sends your topic plus a sample of your own past posts to a model API, so drafts sound like you, with a couple of tone options (punchier, shorter, thread). Build a slot-based queue — preferred weekday posting times from a config file — where drafts fill the next free slot, can be reordered, or pinned to an exact time; support threads with a per-post character counter. Publish on a scheduled loop through the X API, marking each post as sent or failed before it actually posts so nothing double-fires. Pull your own recent post metrics (impressions, likes, replies) on a daily schedule into a simple dashboard: a per-post table and a rolling trend line. Add a copy-to-clipboard fallback per queued post so the tool stays useful without paying for API write access.

Do not build a viral-post library, optimal-timing models, auto-DM or lead-generation features, or multi-account management — those are data and terms-of-service problems, not code, and pretending otherwise wastes real effort. Be blunt in the README that posting through X's API needs a paid tier, and that cost exists before your first scheduled post goes out.

faq.q: Can I import my existing SuperX queue and drafts?
faq.a: Not automatically — there's no structured export of scheduled drafts. Recreating an active queue by hand is realistic, since it's rarely more than a handful of pending posts.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The composer is a responsive web page, usable on a phone for drafting, but there's no dedicated app, and paying for and configuring X's API access is a desktop-and-developer-console task either way.

faq.q: What does it actually cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting plus LLM API usage per draft, typically a few cents — the real cost is X's own paid API write tier, which exists before the first scheduled post goes out and can exceed the flat subscription price depending on volume.

faq.q: What's the one thing that genuinely doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The data. Knowing what performs in a given niche and when to post it comes from years of collected engagement data across many accounts; a personal script only ever has visibility into your own account's numbers.
